15.0.0.en: Moses led the people in praise and glorified God for His great power in His victory over the enemies and the protection of His people, despite the strength of the Egyptian army with its chariots and horsemen, as they all drowned in the sea. This is the first song of praise to the Lord in the Holy Bible, written by Moses, and it speaks of two subjects:

15.0.1.en: 1- God's rescue of His people and the destruction of their enemies (vv. 1-12).

15.0.2.en: 2- A prophecy of their entering Canaan and their victory over its inhabitants (vv. 13-20).

15.1.0.en: Because of Moses' love for God, he loved praising Him until God became his glorification and his joy, so he blessed Him and declared his faith in Him above all the pagan gods.

15.2.0.en: The power of God appeared as a warrior greater than all the warriors of the earth, so His name became the greatest of warriors, that is, able to triumph in all wars however strong the enemies may be. This does not contradict His being the God of heaven, because He disciplines the enemies that perhaps they may repent, and if they exhaust all opportunities for repentance, He destroys them, that perhaps whoever sees them may believe and return to God and enjoy His fatherly tenderness and mercy.

15.3.0.en: The strongest army in the world at that time, the Egyptian army, with its chariots and horses of which it boasts, was drowned.

15.4.1.en: The bodies of the enemies sank like a stone to the bottom of the sea, and they became like stone because their hearts were of stone and refused to believe in God.

15.5.0.en: The right hand represents power, so the power of God is stronger than all the enemies, who signify the demons, and we no longer fear their wars.

15.6.0.en: God's wrath against the wicked consumes them quickly, and He likened them to stubble in the swiftness of its burning.

15.7.0.en: "The blast of thy nostrils": He likens God to a man with a nose from which breath goes out, and because God is strong, His breath is very strong; what is meant is the east wind that dried the sea so that the children of Israel crossed over it. "The waters were gathered together": they began to rise one upon another to become like a wall on both sides.

15.7.1.en: "The floods stood upright": the flowing waters stood upright like a wall on both sides.

15.7.3.en: "The depths were congealed": the waves became solid like a dry wall inside the sea.

15.7.4.en: God sent an east wind that divided the Red Sea, so the waters congealed like a wall on both sides so that the people of God might cross in safety. Thus the power of God that works miracles appears, giving the waters a new nature that is not their own, which is to stand vertically like a wall, and this is against the law of the earth's gravity for liquids. God has done many miracles of this kind, among them His walking, and Peter's, on the water (Mt 14:26, 29).

15.8.0.en: Pharaoh dared in his wickedness to follow the people of God to seize them and return them as slaves to him in Egypt and to kill whoever opposed him, thinking that he was able to overtake them and bring them back as spoil for himself, they and all that was with them. So Satan dares against the children of God, but they defeat him by the power of God.

15.9.0.en: God commanded, and the sea returned as it was after the children of Israel had come out, so the Egyptians drowned and became heavy as lead and clung to the earth as if they were earthly and carnal.

15.10.0.en: God is greater than all the pagan gods in His holiness... praised above all, a worker of miracles that the mind cannot imagine; His servants praise Him with fear, while His enemies tremble and shudder.

15.11.0.en: God stretched out His hand over the sea and it covered the Egyptians, and the sea swallowed them up and they sank to its bottom.

15.12.0.en: God rescued His children from the bondage of Egypt and brought them out to the wilderness of Sinai to worship Him in the tabernacle of meeting, where His holy sanctuary is. He guided them by His mercies and His fatherly tenderness, and had compassion on them because of their faith and their sense of their weakness. He redeemed them by bringing them out of the bondage of Egypt by means of the Passover lamb and His killing of the firstborn of Egypt, and He guided them to walk in the wilderness to Mount Sinai, where He declared to them the commandments and the tabernacle of meeting, and they set it up there.

15.13.0.en: All the nations heard of this miracle, such as the land of Palestine, that is, the land of Canaan, which the children of Israel possessed afterward, and they were very afraid of God and His people.

15.13.1.en: God gives His children awe in the eyes of others, as they feel a wonderful power in them and fear to wrong them despite their weak appearance, because God protects them and makes their enemies fear them.

15.14.0.en: He gives examples of the inhabitants of the Promised Land, namely the Edomites, the Moabites and the Canaanites, who were afraid when they heard of the crossing of the Red Sea and the drowning of the Egyptians.

15.15.0.en: "Thou hast purchased": by Your bringing Your people out of the bondage of Egypt to become a people of Your own.

15.15.1.en: All the peoples of the earth were afraid and became silent as a stone before the power of God that appeared in His people when they crossed the wilderness of Sinai and entered the Promised Land, and when they crossed the Red Sea by a divine miracle and the strongest army in the world, the army of the Egyptians, died before them. This prophecy was fulfilled by the defeat of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan, and Balak king of Moab was troubled by them (Num 21:1-3).

15.16.0.en: The children of Israel did not come out of the bondage of Egypt to live in the wilderness of Sinai but to possess and be established in the land of Canaan, and to build the temple in Jerusalem on Mount Zion to worship the Lord all their days, and that God might reign over the hearts of His children, and that there might come from them Christ, who reigns forever.

15.17.0.en: He presents the summary of the miracle, which is the drowning of the whole Egyptian army and the deliverance of the children of Israel, who crossed into the wilderness of Sinai by walking on dry ground in the midst of the sea.

15.17.1.en: God is able to perform any miracle to rescue and keep His people in every generation, so be at peace and hold fast to your prayers, confident in the power of your God.

15.18.0.en: "The sister of Aaron": she was called so because Aaron was the older in age, although Moses was more famous than he, and out of Moses' humility he did not attribute his sister to himself but to his brother.

15.18.1.en: "Timbrels": round frames of wood with a thin skin stretched over one of their faces, with metal discs fixed to them, so that when struck against the wall these discs or small cymbals move and produce a strong sound and clear tones.

15.18.2.en: "Dances": calm movements offered as worship to God, which were used anciently to express joy and praise to God, as David danced before the ark of the covenant (2 Sam 6:14). This is of course entirely different from worldly dancing, which God hated and because of which Moses destroyed those who danced around the golden calf (ch. 32). The women also took part, led by Miriam the sister of Moses, in praising God, using timbrels as musical instruments to express their joy.

15.19.0.en: Miriam was leading them in praise like Moses her brother, magnifying and blessing God who triumphed over His enemies.

15.19.1.en: Because of the importance of this praise that Moses spoke and Miriam his sister followed in it, the Church takes care to repeat it every day in her Tasbeha and calls it the First Hoos, that is, the first praise, because it declares the power of God with His faithful children, which gives them victory over the demons, gives them spiritual blessings and then brings them into heaven.

15.20.0.en: "Shur": it means a wall, and it lies north of the wilderness of Sinai, and Etham is on its edge, so it is sometimes called the wilderness of Etham, as in (Num 33:6-8) (map 2, p. 93).

15.20.1.en: After the people had glorified God and rejoiced in freedom, they walked three days in the barren wilderness of Sinai, led by the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night, that is, God was leading them, until they reached the wilderness of Shur, a barren wilderness with no water or grass.

15.21.0.en: "Marah": a wilderness whose waters are bitter even now, lying south of the Springs of Moses near the northeastern bank of the Gulf of Suez.

15.21.1.en: The children of Israel reached a wilderness in which there were springs of water, but it was bitter and could not be drunk because of its bitterness, so they called it Marah.

15.22.0.en: The people felt great distress, as they almost died of thirst, and they murmured against Moses their leader and against God.

15.22.1.en: The servant is responsible for those he serves and must bear their murmurings and pray for them, so that God may satisfy them, shepherd them and solve their problems.

15.23.1.en: "There he made for them a statute and an ordinance": that is, the commandment that God spoke in the next verse.

15.23.2.en: "And there he proved them": He allowed them the affliction of the bitter water to show their faith in God or their murmuring.

15.23.3.en: Moses prayed by the power of God, and He answered him and instructed him to cast a tree, or a branch of it, into the bitter water, and it became sweet, and the people drank of it and were satisfied. Thus Moses passed the test successfully because of his faith and his prayer, while the people showed their weakness in their murmuring and lack of faith. And as he cast the tree into the water and it was buried in it and made it sweet, so by the burial of Christ in the tomb He raised us from death and gave us a new, sweet life with Him. The tree signifies the Cross that accomplished our redemption, so we were satisfied with the Holy Spirit, and the placing of the tree in the water signifies the sacrament of Baptism that we received from the blessings of the Cross.

15.24.0.en: God charged the people through Moses to listen to the commandments of God after they had seen His power for the second time since the miracle of the crossing of the Red Sea, and He asked them to obey Him so that they would not be exposed to the diseases that fell on the Egyptians in the ten plagues, but that God would heal them of every disease they might be exposed to, as He healed the bitter water so that it became sweet.

15.25.0.en: "Elim": it means trees, and it is a fertile oasis lying southeast of Marah, that is, inside the wilderness of Sinai and not far from the Gulf of Suez.

15.25.1.en: After the trial of the bitter water, God led them to a fertile region, Elim, in which there were 12 springs of water and which was full of trees, for there were seventy palm trees in it. They signify the twelve tribes and the seventy elders in the Jewish supreme council (the Sanhedrin), and they signify even more the grace of the New Testament, in which there are 12 disciples and 70 apostles.

15.25.2.en: If you endure the trial, you receive blessings from God that you do not expect, so you are satisfied and refreshed by His grace and rejoice with a true joy.

16.0.s.en: (1) The hunger and murmuring of the children of Israel

16.0.0.en: "The wilderness of Sin": it is a desert region lying between Elim on the west and the wilderness of Sinai on the east (map 2, p. 93). What is meant by the wilderness of Sinai is the middle part of the wilderness of Sinai extending east of Suez to the borders of the land of Sinai. The wilderness of Sinai mentioned here extends from the middle to near the south of Sinai. The cloud moved from Elim and they reached the wilderness of Sin as they were walking beside the Red Sea, and there was no food in it. The dough with which they had come out of the land of Egypt had run out, so they became hungry. This was in the second month on the fifteenth day, whereas their departure from the land of Egypt was on the fifteenth day of the first month; that is, they reached the wilderness of Sin about a month after their departure.

16.0.1.en: The details of the journey in the wilderness of Sinai are found in the Book of Numbers (Num 33).

16.1.0.en: The children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron instead of praying, trusting in the power of God who had brought them across the sea.

16.2.0.en: The people spoke to Moses and Aaron and rebuked them for the lack of food and their exposure to death, and they regretted leaving Egypt, remembering the meat and bread they used to eat there and forgetting the humiliation of bondage.

16.2.1.en: Do not seek the places of sin, however rich they may be or however great their material benefits, and however great your need; death with Christ is better than life in sin.

16.3.0.en: God answered the people's murmuring with blessings that cannot be imagined: food coming down from heaven in a very huge quantity covering the ground, so that all the people would be satisfied. Moreover, the food coming down from heaven is given daily, so that a man takes of it what suffices him for the one day. By this God tests the people, whether they will believe His word and obey Him, so that no one stores any of this food, or whether they will disobey Him and not be content with the need of the day. God's testing of His people for forty years in the wilderness after their being baptized in the cloud signifies the temptation of Christ for forty days in the wilderness after His Baptism at the hand of John the Baptist, and as the children of Israel entered the Promised Land after crossing the wilderness, so Christ also began His ministry of preaching and drawing souls after His temptation in the wilderness.

16.4.0.en: "They shall prepare that which they bring in": they make it ready for eating by grinding it and baking it or cooking it in any form (Num 11:8). God commands them to gather on the sixth day enough for two days, so that they may rest on the seventh day and be free for the worship of God.

16.5.0.en: Moses and Aaron knew that God would give meat in the evening, which is the quails (v. 13), coming in great migrating flocks from Europe to central Africa, passing through the wilderness of Sinai in great weariness and flying close to the ground at a height of about one meter, so that they are easy to catch because they fly slowly. This matter of the quails happened either (1) for one day at the beginning of their entering Sinai and then, years later, for a month in the region of Taberah (Num 11), or (2) their words here are about what would happen later, when they ask for meat and He gives them the quails; the details of this story are mentioned in (Num 11). But in the morning of this day, and throughout the forty years, the manna came down like rain from heaven.

16.6.0.en: Moses made clear to them that God would give them meat in the evening, which is the quails, and bread, which is the manna, in the morning, and he declared that he was merely a mediator between them and God, who had heard their murmuring and answered with His tenderness and gave them their needs.

16.7.0.en: Moses and Aaron proclaimed the presence of God and His hearing of the people's murmuring, and asked them to rise and come forward to hear the voice of God.

16.7.1.en: God is present, but you do not feel His presence unless you draw near to Him in prayer, and then you receive His blessings and He forgives you your sins.

16.8.0.en: While Aaron was speaking to the people of what God had commanded him and Moses, and announcing to them the coming down of food from heaven, the glory of God appeared in the cloud; that is, a great cloud, attracting attention, appeared.

16.9.0.en: God spoke from the cloud and the people heard His voice, and perhaps they distinguished the words, or Moses and Aaron did, and told the people that God would give them meat in the evening, which is the quail bird. The flocks of quails came twice: the first time at the beginning of the people's departure into the wilderness, and the second time for a month when they murmured against God because they were weary of the manna, and that was at Taberah. In the morning, God gave them the manna, that is, the bread coming down from heaven.

16.9.1.en: God is long-suffering toward you and answers your murmurings with blessings, that perhaps you may believe in Him, thank Him and apologize for your murmuring.

16.10.s.en: (3) The coming down of the quails and the manna

16.10.0.en: "Came up": flew at a height of about one meter from the ground (Num 11:31). "Quails": a bird resembling the quail and the size of a dove, but its neck and legs are longer than the neck and legs of a dove.

16.10.1.en: What God had said was indeed done, as flocks of quails passed in the evening of the same day, and the people took of them as they wished. In the morning the dew, which carries the manna, covered the wilderness around the children of Israel.

16.11.0.en: In the morning the dew evaporated, and the people found a fine thing covering the ground, resembling flakes or brittle frost, and white in color.

16.12.0.en: The people asked about this thing that covered the ground, and Moses said to them, it is the food that God has given you; therefore it was called manna, and because they did not know what it was they said, "Who is it?"

16.12.1.en: The manna is a symbol of Christ in the following:

16.12.2.en: 1- The manna came down from heaven, as Christ became incarnate and descended from His heaven to live in our midst.

16.12.3.en: 2- The manna is white, as Christ is pure, without sin.

16.12.4.en: 3- The taste of the manna is sweet, like the words of Christ, sweet to the soul.

16.12.5.en: 4- The manna came down after the murmuring of the Jews because they had no food, and it made peace and satisfied them, as Christ by His Incarnation and redemption made reconciliation between God and mankind.

16.12.6.en: 5- The manna came down in the early morning, and the people went out to gather it, or else it melted with the rays of the sun; likewise whoever wants to live with Christ must rise early to Him and put Him before all his worldly concerns.

16.12.7.en: 6- A man gathers of the manna what suffices him for his daily food, just as the Christian must be content in meeting his material needs, not busying himself with storing up or worrying about the future, because he is satisfied with Christ, who satisfies him even if what he has of material things is little.

16.12.8.en: 7- Whoever gathers of the manna more than he needs and keeps it for the next day, it spoils; likewise whoever does not use the means of grace that he knows and the word of God, it condemns him.

16.12.9.en: 8- The people did not know this food, so they said, "Who is it?"; likewise no one can know the essence of Christ, but we know something of His attributes and His relation to us as far as we can understand.

16.12.10.en: 9- They would bake it or cook it, that is, they used fire in cooking it; and Christ also bore sufferings to offer us salvation and spiritual satisfaction.

16.13.0.en: Moses commanded them to take what they needed of this food, and he told them that each one should take the measure of an omer, which equals 2.29 liters, that is, about two and a third liters.

16.13.1.en: God's gifts may seem strange at first because they are higher than worldly blessings, but when you obey God and thank Him, you discover their sweetness more and more. God's arrangements may seem strange or contrary to your planning, but if you accept them with contentment, you discover in time that they are the best thing for you, and satisfy you, and suit your life and lead you toward God.

16.14.0.en: Each one gathered as much as he wished of this food; some gathered much and some little.

16.15.0.en: The surprise appeared when each one measured what he had gathered in order to carry out God's commandment to gather an omer for every person, and they discovered that what they had gathered was an omer for each individual, whether they had gathered much or little.

16.15.1.en: When God blesses your works, He gives you good enough for you, and even if it seems little, you will be satisfied with it.

16.16.0.en: Moses commanded them not to leave any of it until the next morning, but some of them doubted the coming down of the manna the next day and kept some of it, but were surprised to find it full of worms and loathsome, not to be eaten, so Moses was angry with them because of the weakness of their faith and their disobedience to God.

16.17.0.en: The people continued to gather every day what they needed of the manna. The strange thing is that when the sun rose the manna melted and became liquid, and the earth drank it.

16.17.1.en: If you do not rise early to God to receive His blessing in prayer, the blessing may depart from you and your opportunity be lost, as the manna would melt and be gone.

16.18.s.en: (5) The manna does not come down on the Sabbath

16.18.0.en: The people obeyed and gathered on the sixth day twice what they gathered on the other days, because the manna would not come down on the Sabbath. The rulers of the people told Moses what they had done, to make sure that this was the command of the Lord, so that he would not be angry with them as happened when some of them kept some of it until the next day and it bred worms (v. 20).

16.19.0.en: Moses said to them, cook it so that you may eat of it in the way you wish, and keep the rest until the next day, and it will not spoil, so that you may be free on the seventh day for the worship of God.

16.19.1.en: Take care of Sunday, the Lord's Day, and increase your prayers and good works, remembering that on this day Christ rose to give you a new life; make it a day distinguished from the rest of your days, so that you may feel God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

16.20.0.en: God's word was indeed fulfilled, that the manna that was kept would not spoil with stench or worms the next day, that is, the Sabbath.

16.21.0.en: Moses told them to eat of the manna that was kept on the Sabbath, because no manna would come down on this day; so this became a custom with them, to rest on the seventh day to be free for worship.

16.21.1.en: Be sure that God provides for your needs, and your being occupied with His worship will not diminish the material blessing but will increase it.

16.22.s.en: (6) The people's disobedience in going out to gather the manna

16.22.0.en: Some of the Jews did not believe God's word and went out to make sure for themselves that there was no manna on the seventh day. This shows their doubt of God's commands and their attachment to material things.

16.23.0.en: "Abide ye every man in his place": what is meant is that they should not go out in the morning to gather manna but be free on this day for the worship of God, leaving all material work, moving only short distances if necessary, as the elders of the Jews determined.

16.23.1.en: God reproached the people in His speech with Moses because they had gone out on the Sabbath to gather manna although He had commanded them not to go out, so He rebuked their disobedience.

16.24.0.en: After this incident the whole people obeyed the word of God and did not move on the Sabbath to gather manna.

16.25.0.en: He describes the taste of the manna as sweet, like wafers made with honey, and its form as small grains like coriander seed. The Book of Wisdom tells us how every person who ate the manna felt a particular taste as he desired, and this is a wonderful mystery, that the manna had different tastes according to the desire of each one.

16.25.1.en: Believe the word of the Holy Bible even if it is above your mind, and do not transgress its commandments, so that you may enjoy its blessings and God's pleasure with you.

16.26.1.en: "The testimony": the ark of the covenant in the tabernacle of meeting.

16.26.2.en: God commanded Moses that they keep a quantity of manna in a vessel, so that throughout history they would remember the miracle of the Lord in feeding them in the wilderness. They kept the manna afterward in a golden vessel inside the ark of the covenant. The quantity of manna that was kept was the measure of an omer, that is, about 2.29 liters.

16.26.3.en: The keeping of the manna in the golden pot signifies:

16.26.4.en: 1- The Incarnation of Christ, for as the manna came down from heaven, God came down and became incarnate in the fullness of time.

16.26.5.en: 2- The manna signifies Holy Communion from the Body and Blood of Christ.

16.26.6.en: 3- The golden pot signifies the Virgin who carried Christ in her womb.

16.27.0.en: God continued to send the manna daily to feed His people for 40 years in the wilderness of Sinai until they reached the Promised Land, where they found cultivated land and ate of its fruits, and the manna ceased. Moses said this by the spirit of prophecy, for the manna ceased when Joshua entered the Promised Land and they began to eat the fruits of the land; in addition, it may have ceased for the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, who took possession east of the Jordan in the days of Moses (Num 32, Josh 13).

16.27.1.en: God's gifts to you continue as long as you feel your need of them, but when you find material things to lean on, God stops His gifts. So do not be distressed by the lack of some resources or the fewness of friends and loved ones, because God Himself compensates you for them, and He is your true strength and your personal friend.

16.28.0.en: The omer equals, as we mentioned, 2.29 liters, and it is a tenth of a known Jewish measure, the ephah, which equals 22.9 liters.

16.28.1.en: The symbols of the manna: we note from the above that the manna signifies:

16.28.2.en: 1- The Incarnation of Christ, for He said of Himself, "I am the living bread which came down from heaven" (Jn 6:51).

16.28.3.en: 2- The Body and Blood of Christ, for He said, "the bread that I will give is my flesh" (Jn 6:51). And He also said, "Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you" (Jn 6:53).

16.28.4.en: 3- It is the glory that we receive in heaven, for He said, "To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna" (Rev 2:17). The spiritual meanings of the manna:

16.28.5.en: 1- Faith and reliance on God, who provides for our needs daily.

16.28.6.en: 2- Obedience to God, whose commands exceed our mental comprehension: their going out every day to gather the manna, not keeping any of it for the next day except on the sixth day, and not going out on the seventh day.

16.28.7.en: 3- Rising early to God before any work, in prayer and reading His Holy Bible, as they used to rise early before sunrise to gather the manna before it melted in the heat of the sun.

16.28.8.en: 4- The importance of work and spiritual striving, which appeared in their going out every morning to gather it.

16.28.9.en: 5- The blessing of God, for what each person gathered was enough, whether he gathered little or much.

16.28.10.en: 6- God's keeping of our food and our needs, for the manna, which melts in the light rays of the sun in the early morning, remains firm and produces different cakes and baked goods after the women put it on the strong fire (Wis 16:27).

16.28.11.en: 7- The variety of God's blessings to man so that he may delight in them, for the taste of the manna for each one who ate it was according to what he desired, that is, its flavor differed from one person to another according to the liking of each one (Wis 16:25).

16.28.12.en: 8- Contentment, for God gave them one food and did not give them different kinds of foods, and because of their contentment He made His food differ according to the desire of each one. This is what calls the faithful to fasting and detachment, so that God blesses the little they have and it becomes sweet and satisfying to them.
